transcript: As of seeing it again at fringe, I've seen to free a Mockingbird four different times, and it continues to hit me emotionally every single time. And that says basically everything you need to know about this piece. Stafrya Mokingbird is a one person show written and performed by Grace O'keeffe about three different generations of both love and grief. So much of this piece dives into our relationships, especially with family members, based off of the stories that we choose to and to not tell. And there is such a special uniqueness to the vulnerability that Grace brings to this piece, from the moment that she enters the stage to the moment that she leaves, and the way that she interacts with the audience that makes this so unique from other one person shows that I've seen. And even though the show deals with a lot of very dark subject matters, it is very, very funny. For anybody who follows Grace Aki on social media, you know that she's an incredibly funny person, and that definitely comes through in this show. And that blend of vulnerability and comedy is what makes the ending of this play land as well as it does. This show is absolutely a must see if you have a complicated relationship with your family, if you are grieving the loss of a loved one, if you love good storytelling, if you just love good theater. In fact, this is just a must see in general. The Free Mockingbird is currently playing at the Fringe Festival in Edinburgh at the Royal Scots Club, which is a little bit of a trek in Newtown. It is worth the trek. I literally had to go from see this at the Royal Scots Club all the way to Summerhall. I took an Uber. It was worth it. I cannot recommend this show enough. If you are not able to see it at fringe, then I highly recommend just following Grace Aki on all social media platforms because 1. She's a very entertaining person and 2. I have no doubt that she will be performing this again in the future. So definitely definitely definitely. If you get a chance I give her a follow.
